- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 10–20% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 15–30% to avoid overreaction.  
- If recent history shows sharp upward spikes (e.g., 2+ consecutive days > 2.0) and forecast is still low, add a 15–25% lagged overshoot correction.  
- If forecast consistently underestimates true values (especially in 30d horizon), apply a 5–10% mean reversion bias toward historical 18-day average.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and forecast is erratic, apply a smoothing filter to reduce volatility and align with recent trend.  
- For 30d forecasts with high variance or extreme outliers, cap forecast at ±20% of 18-day moving average to avoid runaway spikes.
